zh-CN.AI teams need golden paths for data acce: AI teams need golden paths for data access, model calls, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring. Otherwise every prototype becomes custom infrastructure.
zh-CN.The practical reason this topic is getti: The practical reason this topic is getting attention in 2026 is simple: AI work is spreading across departments faster than shared infrastructure can keep up. For platform teams supporting multiple AI product squads, the question is no longer whether the trend is interesting. The question is where it changes daily work enough to justify new process, budget, or risk review.
zh-CN.The common failure mode is forcing each: The common failure mode is forcing each team to invent its own data connectors, prompt logs, evals, and deployment path. That mistake usually happens when a trend is treated as a feature checklist instead of an operating change. The technology may be new, but the weak point is often ownership, permissions, data quality, recovery, or review.
zh-CN.Before picking a vendor or writing code,: Before picking a vendor or writing code, decide which capabilities should be self-service and which require review. A clear first decision keeps the team from mixing experiments, production systems, sensitive data, and customer promises into one blurry rollout.
zh-CN.Start small: build a paved path for expe: Start small: build a paved path for experiments, then gate production with security and eval checks. Keep the first version narrow enough that success and failure are both visible. That makes it easier to compare quality, cost, latency, privacy, and support load before expanding the workflow.
zh-CN.A mature workflow produces a platform ba: A mature workflow produces a platform backlog covering datasets, model routing, secrets, evals, and observability. It should be easy for someone outside the implementation team to inspect what happened, understand why it happened, and decide whether the result is reliable enough to act on.
zh-CN.Set a review date, a measurable success: Set a review date, a measurable success criterion, and a rollback path before launch. If the platform engineering for AI workflow does not improve the actual decision, reduce risk, save time, or create a clearer user experience, keep it in research instead of forcing it into production.
